title: Behind-the-Scenes Star Wars Collection Appears Online
summary:
A collection of behind-the-scenes pictures and videos from special-effects artist Phil Tippett’s film work has appeared on the Internet Archive. News of the collection circulated during the week before October 4, 2026, including a social media post on October 1.

Tippett and his team worked on films including Star Wars, Jurassic Park and RoboCop. He is especially known for using stop-motion animation to bring imaginary creatures to life. In stop motion, an object is moved a little between photographs. When the pictures play in order, the object seems to move.

The collection appears to come from a folder of CDs bought by an unnamed fan at a sale after Tippett’s Berkeley, California, studio closed in August 2026. The buyer said they noticed that some material was not available online and wanted to preserve its high-resolution detail. They copied the contents and uploaded files representing 90 different discs.

The Star Wars material includes pictures from the making of the cantina scene in A New Hope, along with images of puppets and stop-motion creatures. There are also glimpses of the film’s small holographic chess figures.

Other files show work on RoboCop, creature textures from Hellboy and computer wireframe models from Jurassic Park. The collection also includes photographs from animator Ray Harryhausen’s 90th birthday.

Although his studio has closed, Tippett has said he is not quite ready to retire.
why_it_matters: The uploaded collection provides a view of film-effects work and preserves material the buyer said was not already available online.
